headline_marked: Ex-Army Chief [[Shafiuddin Ahmed skips ACC summons]] and asks for 30 days
headline: Ex-Army Chief Shafiuddin Ahmed skips ACC summons and asks for 30 days
summary: Former Army Chief General SM Shafiuddin Ahmed failed to appear before the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) on Monday for questioning regarding illegal asset accumulation.
details: Former Army Chief General SM Shafiuddin Ahmed did not appear before the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) on Monday for questioning regarding allegations of acquiring illegal assets through corruption.
The ACC Deputy Director, Md. Aktarul Islam, confirmed that Shafiuddin Ahmed was scheduled to appear at the ACC's head office in Segunbagicha, Dhaka, but instead applied for a 30-day time extension.
The commission had summoned him on August 30, via a letter from Director Mo. Abul Hasnat, requiring him to appear at 12:30 PM on Monday with a copy of his National Identity Card.
The summons notice stated that hearing and recording his statement is 'essential' for a fair and proper investigation into the corruption allegations.
An investigation team led by Director Mo. Abul Hasnat has been conducting an investigation into the corruption allegations against the former Army Chief since December 14 last year.
General SM Shafiuddin Ahmed served as the Chief of Army Staff from June 24, 2021, to June 23, 2024, during the tenure of the Awami League government.
caption:
A former Army Chief skips his ACC summons. He's now asking for a 30-day extension.

Former Army Chief General SM Shafiuddin Ahmed did not appear before the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) on Monday for questioning regarding allegations of acquiring illegal assets through corruption.

The ACC Deputy Director, Md. Aktarul Islam, confirmed that Shafiuddin Ahmed was scheduled to appear at the ACC's head office in Segunbagicha, Dhaka, but instead applied for a 30-day time extension.

The commission had summoned him on August 30, via a letter from Director Mo. Abul Hasnat, requiring him to appear at 12:30 PM on Monday with a copy of his National Identity Card.

The summons notice stated that hearing and recording his statement is 'essential' for a fair and proper investigation into the corruption allegations.

An investigation team led by Director Mo. Abul Hasnat has been conducting an investigation into the corruption allegations against the former Army Chief since December 14 last year.

General SM Shafiuddin Ahmed served as the Chief of Army Staff from June 24, 2021, to June 23, 2024, during the tenure of the Awami League government.

#Bangladesh #ACC #CorruptionInvestigation #ArmyChief #Dhaka #News

Source: Prothom Alo, Dhaka Tribune
